events.title: The Girl Behind the Contact Sheet

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At the card shop, a very short, pale-blonde woman studies two expensive cards through the glass. A garment bag hangs from her shoulder beside a scuffed deck case.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You look like you're choosing between rent and a rare card.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: Rent is already paid. That's why I can look at the card.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Do I know you? I saw your face on a poster downtown.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: Probably. I'm Lyla. I model. It's a job, not a calling.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: They keep asking for my face and my abs. Being 148 centimeters helps with some looks. They make clothes fit me, not the other way around.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: And you like it?

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: I like how the photographs turn out. I don't love the hours. I'd rather spend the money on cards.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She considers you with a nearly unreadable expression, then holds up two Eevee cards like a casting decision.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: Which one looks more dangerous? There's a correct answer.

choices.label: Judge the cards by their playability
choices.reply: Good. You're looking at what they do, not just their faces.

choices.label: Offer to help carry her garment bag
choices.reply: If you're serious, yes. My arms are done posing for today.

choices.label: Say the poster didn't capture her best feature
choices.reply: Careful. You haven't seen my deck yet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Lyla texts you a location and a single instruction: 'Bring water.' The cafe's upstairs room has become a temporary studio for an adult streetwear lookbook.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: The stylist wants me to look spontaneous. We've done six takes of 'spontaneous'.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You seem more comfortable between shots.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: Because nobody asks me to perform being interesting while I'm drinking water.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She cycles through layered hoodies, a sleeveless tank, wide-leg jeans and colorful sneakers. Every outfit has been fitted to her compact proportions; the stylist checks the hem instead of asking her to change her posture.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: They book me for petite streetwear. It's useful. Sometimes people forget petite doesn't mean I want to look like a kid.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: What do you want the pictures to say?

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: That I know exactly where I stand. Also that the shoes look good.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She asks you to hold a reflector—not to direct her body, but to tell her when the light finally looks real.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: Tell me when you can recognize me in the photo. Not just the clothes.

choices.label: Describe the lighting and let Lyla choose the pose
choices.reply: Thank you. That's actual feedback, not somebody telling me to smile.

choices.label: Back her up when the stylist suggests a childish pose
choices.reply: I'm twenty. Cute styling is fine; pretending I'm twelve isn't.

choices.label: Tell her the camera has trouble keeping up with her
choices.reply: You rehearsed that line. ...Not bad.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: You join Lyla at a studio lobby after a fitness campaign fitting. Her athletic outfit is practical: a fitted training top, running shorts and sneakers. On the tablet, the campaign copy is another matter.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: They want to sell 'perfect abs in ten days.' They hired me because my stomach already looks like this. That's not a promise you can put on a poster.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: So don't sign it.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: I need the paycheck. I don't need my face attached to a lie.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She scratches out a line in the brief and writes an alternative about movement and comfort. A coordinator hesitates over the change.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: I don't mind them photographing my body. I mind people pretending it came from a product.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: What would make the shoot worth doing?

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: A truthful caption. Clothes that fit. And enough money for those Neo cards I've been tracking.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She turns the tablet toward you, asking for a second opinion on her proposed terms.

choices.label: Help her rewrite the claim clearly
choices.reply: It sounds like me. That's what I wanted.

choices.label: Offer to stay while she negotiates
choices.reply: You don't have to speak for me. Just stay. That helps.

choices.label: Say her strongest feature is knowing her worth
choices.reply: ...I like that better than a compliment about my face.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: An evening editorial shoot ends near the arcade. Lyla has swapped a tailored jacket and pleated skirt for her usual cat-print top and baggy jeans. She carries the garment bag like it's twice her height.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: Six outfits, nine hours, one photographer calling everything 'effortless.' My feet disagree.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You still stopped by the arcade.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: I had a good shoot. I wanted a good evening too.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She chooses the most difficult machine and wins without speaking, then loses the next round while trying to explain an Umbreon combo.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: That's embarrassing. In front of my own witness.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: A rematch?

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: No. A match with actual cards. I don't want another camera deciding when I'm impressive.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For the first time tonight, her expression softens as she opens her deck case. Winning a game seems to interest her far more than winning a casting.

choices.label: Play a relaxed match and let her talk strategy
choices.reply: Finally. A place where the numbers make sense.

choices.label: Ask which photograph she was proudest of
choices.reply: The one where I wasn't trying to look taller. It felt honest.

choices.label: Offer a wager: the winner picks the next outing
choices.reply: That sounds suspiciously like a date. I'm listening.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A small outdoor fashion editorial uses soft summer layers, colorful jackets and casual dresses. The photographer has been asking Lyla to smile for twenty minutes. Her expression remains precise and professional.

lines.speaker: Photographer
lines.text: Just one real smile, Lyla. Give us something alive.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: You can't order one like coffee.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: During a break, an unexpected gust carries the carefully arranged paper backdrop into the bushes. You and Lyla chase it; an assistant's tiny dog steals a ribbon and refuses to surrender.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: I think the dog has been promoted to creative director.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: ...He'd do a better job with the call sheet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then she laughs—openly, without checking who is watching. Her whole face changes. The photographer lowers the camera instead of taking the shot.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: What? Did I get something on my face?

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: No. Nothing like that.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: Good. Because that one wasn't for the campaign.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She meets your eyes for a second longer than usual, the trace of a smile still there.

choices.label: Help retrieve the backdrop without turning her laugh into a performance
choices.reply: Thanks for not making a thing of it. I actually had fun.

choices.label: Tell her she should decide when photographs get taken
choices.reply: That's exactly what people forget. You remembered.

choices.label: Admit her genuine laugh caught you off guard
choices.reply: Then don't tell the photographer. He'll try to book it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A magazine has offered Lyla a cover. The proposed styling mixes youthful streetwear for adult readers, a tailored suit and a bright sleeveless summer look. This time she has approval over every outfit.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: Biggest fee I've had. They also want to call me 'the girl who never smiles.'

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Does that bother you?

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: It makes me sound like a prop. I smile when something is funny. I just don't do it on command.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She lays out contact sheets. In one, the small model looks powerful against a vast studio backdrop. In another, she sits cross-legged on the floor after the shoot, sorting Pokémon cards.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: The first one gets the cover. The second one is my favorite. That's the person who gets to keep the paycheck.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: What are you going to do with it?

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: Rent. Savings. A card I absolutely cannot justify buying. In that order.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: And maybe... dinner with someone who doesn't ask me to be camera-ready.

choices.label: Support her decision to negotiate the headline
choices.reply: They can have the cover. They don't get to invent my personality.

choices.label: Offer to celebrate after the deadline, no cameras
choices.reply: That sounds like the first good appointment on my calendar.

choices.label: Ask whether the dinner invitation is for you
choices.reply: I hoped you'd figure it out without making me say it twice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The cover is out. Lyla arrives at a quiet café in her favorite jeans and sleeveless cat top, carrying a small envelope and her deck box.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: I signed the new contract. Fewer shoots, better terms. I can afford to say no sometimes.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: And the envelope?

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: The photo they didn't publish. I asked for a print.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It shows Lyla after the cameras stopped, laughing with a deck of cards in her hands. She turns the photo facedown, a little embarrassed.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: I don't hate modeling. I like the pictures. I just want to decide what happens outside them.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: What do you want now?

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: Another match. More cards. People who can sit beside me when nothing interesting is happening.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: You, if you want. Not because somebody asked us to look good together.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A rare, quiet smile reaches her eyes while she waits for your answer.

choices.label: Tell her you want to see where this goes together
choices.reply: Then stay after the café closes. I don't think I'm done talking to you.

choices.label: Promise you'll remain her friend and favorite practice partner
choices.reply: Good. No grand speeches. Just show up with your deck.

choices.label: Say she gets to choose her next chapter
choices.reply: I will. And I like that you're in it without trying to write it for me.

events.title: A Hem and a Deck Box

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Lyla is sitting on a low stool with a roll of hem tape and a fashion sample jacket.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: They size everything around tall mannequins. I brought tape. Also my deck.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Which one is harder to make fit?

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: The jacket. The deck actually listens.

choices.label: Help adjust the sleeve length
choices.reply: You're a more useful assistant than half the studio.

choices.label: Ask why she keeps the original fit notes
choices.reply: Because next time I want them to remember I'm the client too.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: After a sportswear shoot, Lyla rests on a bench in a loose jacket and sneakers, eating a sandwich.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: They liked how my abs photographed. Then they tried to schedule another shoot over lunch.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Did you let them?

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: No. My stomach has more important plans right now.

choices.label: Share lunch and leave work talk behind
choices.reply: Excellent. Finally, a break that's actually a break.

choices.label: Agree that a job shouldn't own her schedule
choices.reply: The contract covers hours. It doesn't cover my whole life.

events.title: Two Versions of the Same Picture

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Lyla shows you a contact sheet: an immaculate editorial pose and a candid photo taken while she was fixing her shoe.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: The first one is good for the client. The second feels like me.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Which one would you keep?

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: You already know. I wanted to hear your answer anyway.

choices.label: Choose the candid and explain why
choices.reply: Yeah. That's the one I kept too.

choices.label: Say both can be valuable in different ways
choices.reply: That's a sensible answer. Annoyingly sensible.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Lyla is opening a small card shop parcel beside the arcade machines. She looks more excited than she did on any magazine cover.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: The shoot paid. The rent is covered. This is the part I was waiting for.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Is that an Umbreon?

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: Don't make me say how much it cost. Ask me to duel instead.

choices.label: Challenge her with your own deck
choices.reply: Deal. Winner gets bragging rights, not my card.

choices.label: Ask what makes Umbreon her favorite
choices.reply: It can take over a whole game without making a scene. I relate.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A delayed payment notice lights up Lyla's phone while she's pricing a Neo booster.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: They can book me three months ahead but take forever to pay. I'm charging them for the reminder.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Sounds like you know what you want.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: She closes the invoice and returns to comparing cards, a little less tense now.

choices.label: Stay with her for a moment
choices.reply: You can stay. I wasn't in a hurry to be alone.

choices.label: Respect her decision
choices.reply: Thanks. It's nice not having to explain every choice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At a summer catalog fitting, Lyla stands beside a rack of light dresses and cropped jackets.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: Petite is a clothing category, not an invitation to treat me like a little girl. The second jacket fits, at least.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Sounds like you know what you want.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: She chooses an adult streetwear combination and leaves the first jacket on the rack.

choices.label: Stay with her for a moment
choices.reply: You can stay. I wasn't in a hurry to be alone.

choices.label: Respect her decision
choices.reply: Thanks. It's nice not having to explain every choice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Lyla has been shooting sneakers in a bright windbreaker and loose shorts. The stylist resets the laces for the sixth time.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: Apparently the left shoelace is the main character. I thought they hired me for the shoes.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Sounds like you know what you want.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: You help retrieve a runaway lace clip, and she awards you a silent nod.

choices.label: Stay with her for a moment
choices.reply: You can stay. I wasn't in a hurry to be alone.

choices.label: Respect her decision
choices.reply: Thanks. It's nice not having to explain every choice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Lyla scrolls through proofs from a studio campaign, pausing on an over-edited portrait.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: That doesn't look like my face anymore. The lighting was beautiful. Why erase it?

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Sounds like you know what you want.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: She sends a concise note requesting a natural edit and finally puts away her phone.

choices.label: Stay with her for a moment
choices.reply: You can stay. I wasn't in a hurry to be alone.

choices.label: Respect her decision
choices.reply: Thanks. It's nice not having to explain every choice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Lyla spreads two sleeve designs across the arcade table: matte charcoal and glossy violet.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: The dark ones make Umbreon look terrifying. The violet ones look like I'm trying too hard.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Sounds like you know what you want.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: You settle on charcoal and she slides one sleeve across the table for you to test.

choices.label: Stay with her for a moment
choices.reply: You can stay. I wasn't in a hurry to be alone.

choices.label: Respect her decision
choices.reply: Thanks. It's nice not having to explain every choice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A stylist calls for a reset. Lyla sits on a folding chair in a tailored vest and wide-leg trousers, quietly eating a sandwich.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: They asked me to be 'effortless' again. This sandwich is the only effortless thing here.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Sounds like you know what you want.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: She goes back to work when the break ends, but slips you a spare fruit juice first.

choices.label: Stay with her for a moment
choices.reply: You can stay. I wasn't in a hurry to be alone.

choices.label: Respect her decision
choices.reply: Thanks. It's nice not having to explain every choice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: An advertisement featuring Lyla shines from the shop window while the real Lyla walks past carrying a deck box.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: That version of me has flawless lighting. This version has a winning hand. I know which one I'd pick.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Sounds like you know what you want.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: She taps the window once, then heads inside with you.

choices.label: Stay with her for a moment
choices.reply: You can stay. I wasn't in a hurry to be alone.

choices.label: Respect her decision
choices.reply: Thanks. It's nice not having to explain every choice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Lyla studies two offers on her phone: a large campaign with poor terms, and a smaller shoot with creative input.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: The smaller client pays on time and doesn't call me 'adorably tiny.' Not a hard choice.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Sounds like you know what you want.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: She declines the larger offer and orders another coffee without looking back.

choices.label: Stay with her for a moment
choices.reply: You can stay. I wasn't in a hurry to be alone.

choices.label: Respect her decision
choices.reply: Thanks. It's nice not having to explain every choice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Lyla leans over the studio table in a black velvet editorial dress, looking back toward the camera.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: The photographer says that's the last shot. That's what he said twenty minutes ago.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You can leave the studio whenever the contract says we're done. The picture doesn't get to decide.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: Ask whether she wants a break

choices.label: You noticed. Yeah. Five minutes would be good.
choices.reply: Tell her the photograph feels like her

choices.label: Maybe. I wasn't trying to please anyone in that one.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The next setup is a close portrait in soft studio light. Lyla studies the camera with her usual half-lidded expression.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: They want a dreamy look. Apparently that means thinking about absolutely nothing.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You look like you're thinking about your next card purchase.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: Correct. That's my most natural expression.

choices.label: Ask which shot she would choose
choices.reply: The one where I look like myself, not their idea of me.

choices.label: Offer to review the contact sheet with her
choices.reply: Good. Tell me if they retouch my face into somebody else.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A stylist brings a coordinated pale outfit for the third setup. Lyla checks the styling and the photographer's reference images before stepping into the lights.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: They've pinned everything twice. I just want the outfit to fit properly.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: The brief said editorial. You should get to decide what feels comfortable.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: Exactly. I'm a model, not a mannequin.

choices.label: Ask whether she approves the styling
choices.reply: After one adjustment. I'm keeping the jacket where I want it.

choices.label: Ask if the campaign pays well
choices.reply: Enough to pay my bills and maybe buy that Umbreon.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: After the final setup, Lyla sits on the studio floor in her styled outfit and sneakers. The lights are still warm, but the crew is packing away the equipment.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: Don't tell them I'm still here. They'll invent another shot.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: I thought you liked how the photos turned out.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: I do. I also like the part when I can stop posing.

choices.label: Offer to stay while she chooses her favorite photo
choices.reply: You can stay. Just don't pick the one where they told me to smile.

choices.label: Suggest a card match after the shoot
choices.reply: Now that's a reason to get up. Give me two minutes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The studio is almost empty. In the last warm light of the day, Lyla sits on a black stool wearing a loose white shirt and heavy boots. The laptop beside her shows a grid of contact sheets.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Still working? I thought the shoot ended an hour ago.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: The camera stopped. The choosing didn't. They want the picture where I look most approachable.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Which one would you choose?

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: The one where I look comfortable. I was waiting for them to stop telling me how to sit.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She turns the laptop so you can compare the polished selects with a quieter, unplanned frame. Her eyes settle on the latter.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: I don't hate modeling. I just want the final photo to feel like I was there, not like someone invented me.

choices.label: Let Lyla choose the image that feels right
choices.reply: Thanks. I think I already knew. I just wanted someone to ask me what I thought.

choices.label: Ask what she wants to do after the studio closes
choices.reply: Cards. Dinner. Preferably both, in that order. You can come if you want.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Lyla turns her camera preview toward you. A test frame from a recent shoot is still on the screen.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: The photographer called this one a test. I like it more than the finished selects.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You look comfortable. Like you forgot to pose for a second.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: Maybe I did. I wasn't thinking about what my hands were supposed to do.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Then keep it. It feels more like you.

lines.speaker: lyla
lines.text: I will. It can stay in my own folder, without a client attached to it.

choices.label: Tell her not every good picture needs to become work
choices.reply: Good. I don't want every part of my life to become a portfolio.

choices.label: Say the relaxed expression suits her
choices.reply: That's because I wasn't trying to look any particular way.
